strings.KEYITEM_CURSEDBOOK_LORE:
Nobody understands the importance of the research of local religions. Think of what we wouldn’t have learned from the Jax-Tu Empire had we glanced over the religious implications of their society. This book, taken from the ruins of some sort of shrine here on Petrichor V, will provide a great insight into the culture on this planet.
-
As of late I have been hearing whispers behind my back. They think I don’t hear them? I do. They don’t understand, but soon they will. This research is important! I have recovered more pages, and with them I will further understand this N’kuhana.
-
I have mostly recovered the pages now. I understand it now. I hear her will. However, I still hear them mocking me. Laughing now. LAUGHING. They’ll never understand. The book grants me strength. Strength grants power. Through power, I command death. Through death, our chains are broken. N’kuhana shall free us. Weshan.
-
The blood is so warm. Like a warm blanket She has wrapped upon me as they leave this world and join her. I sent them all to her. The final mercy I could enact upon them.  They wouldn’t listen so I would free them. Finally, the laughter ceases. Now I can finally free myself.

strings.CURSEDBOOK_SPELL_DIE_LORE:
"Oh, death! Glorious death! It is nothing to fear, my faithful, not at all. Death is a part of life, and it all falls under her loving gaze. To die for our Lady of Balance is to perform the greatest act of servitude of all - the scales are tipped, and only through sacrifice may the imbalance be corrected. 

When all your deeds have been fulfilled, remember this teaching: there is always one more to turn your knife against, even amongst a group of one. Only in death will you be ushered into her embrace."

-Teachings of G'ratha Kormat, Speaker of Her Concepts, Sermon XXVII

strings.CURSEDBOOK_SPELL_CLARITY_LORE:
"The eyes of the common folk are shrouded by this world's lies. So too are yours, initiates, but through our Lady of Balance can that veil be lifted! When you see a law, you see something absolute. A wall that cannot be crossed without a generous tithe of coin. And yet, those with the coin pass freely. Why, just yesterday, some of my friends regalled me with a tale that the bigwigs in UES were caught embezzling funds into some personal project. And their punishment? A 300 thousand credit fine, barely a fraction of their vast fortunes. It is there, initiates, that the lie is exposed! A law is not absolute if one can simply pay their way out of justice! The absolute can be defied! But, that makes one wonder. What other absolutes can one defy...? Could one, say, ignore the laws of... commerce? Physics? Mortality...? I leave you with that question, my faithful, and bid you all a fine evening."

-Teachings of G'ratha Kormat, Speaker of Her Concepts, Sermon XXIV

strings.CURSEDBOOK_SPELL_PURIFY_LORE:
"As we delve deeper into her teachings, you will begin to see the truth of this world. This vision, this Insight, will allow you to better understand her concepts. Meditate on it, initiates, and study its intricacies so you may deepen your connection to the Lady of Balance. 

However, remember to take days of rest - remove yourself from your Insight and view the world as an outsider would. Knowledge and experience of the mortal world helps frame your Insight, and with that context you may better appreciate her teachings. Our greatest teaching; Weshan! "All in balance"."

-Teachings of G'ratha Kormat, Speaker of Her Concepts, Sermon II

strings.CURSEDBOOK_SPELL_SUMMONFERALTODDLERS_LOR:
"Never think yourself alone, initiates. Followers of our Lady of Balance walk amongst you in all circles of life, whether you - or they - know it. Every mortal contributes to the balancing of the scales, in some way or another. Whether it be stomping an insect, driving a knife into the gut of an innocent, or vanquishing a mighty evil... The scales MUST be balanced, and every soul may pay our Lady of Balance their respects. So thus, my faithful, remember; when you are in great need, call out! Let your voice be heard by our Lady, and She will answer. Her followers, no matter where they may be, will come to answer your call."

- Teachings of G'ratha Kormat, Speaker of Her Concepts, Sermon XXIV

strings.CURSEDBOOK_SPELL_TEAMINVISIBILITY_LORE:
"Outsiders will not understand our devotion to our Lady of Balance. Exercise caution, initiates; spread her word to those willing to listen, but do not speak carelessly. 

There are those who fear her concepts and will see us and naught but murderers, psychopaths. Remember well to walk hidden amongst the unbelievers, but do not judge them. They are blind to her concepts, but they will learn. They will learn."

-Teachings of G'ratha Kormat, Speaker of Her Concepts, Sermon IV

strings.CURSEDBOOK_SPELL_UPGRADEITEM_LORE:
"It is said that we are special because of our power to shape our environment. To make tools and use them to our advantage. And it is this power that allowed us travel beyond our wildest dreams, see things that can only be described as fantastical, and spread our Lady of Balance's opinions to all who would listen! But it is also this power that tipped the scales. As we made, as our standard of living increased, the balance of this world was left askew. There are billions, nay, TRILLIONS of souls, waiting to fall into her embrace! How could it come to this, I ask you? I will tell you: the power to create! The power of intelligence! It brought us up from the mud, yes, but we have squandered this gift! Abused it! And now, our Lady demands penance. Only then shall you find peace as the scales are balanced once more." 

- Teachings of G'ratha Kormat, Speaker of Her Concepts, Sermon XXI

strings.CURSEDBOOK_SPELL_WARPGATE_LORE:
"The power of belief is something you must NEVER underestimate, initiates. Sure, the dream of just one individual is just a drop of water, but when that dream is shared amongst many it becomes a mighty river! My old friend, Sigibold, and I discussed this concept at length. Faith allows a mere whelp to cross mountains; the spirit is nurtured by faith, and this nourishment opens your mind to her concepts. Food and water become trivial. When you are lost in the dark, simply defer to our Lady of Balance, perform your meditations, and the way shall be revealed. Your faith will harden and your body shall follow its example."

“Run. Run. Run. Echoing in her head, she figured this gift came with a price but couldn’t pinpoint what it was. 

All her life, she never would have been able to participate in these festival races due to her physical condition. In searching for a cure, some people she knew pointed her in the direction of a small group that met every weekend. Though strange, they welcomed her into their activities and opened her eyes to another world of possibilities. 

The prayer was simple, and after repeating it for 3 months, she got her miracle. 

Run. Run. Run. She was catching up to the runner in 3rd position. Faster. Faster. Faster. Just as she reached the heels of the other runner, something happened. Sarah blacked out for a second, and then she was suddenly ahead, encroaching on 2nd place. 

The audience started to get louder. Was that encouragement? Gaining speed, Sarah closed the gap, then... 

Blackout. 

1st place was in view now. She couldn’t believe it. Wait, was that blood on her hands? 

The spectators looked like they were evacuating... 

Run. Run. RUN. She passed the finish line, but couldn’t stop...” 

-N'tormat Apocryphals, Parable XXIII

strings.ITEM_CAUSTICPHEROMONES_LORE:
"Chained to the ritual stone was the blasphemer Sankor Velliche. Accused of violating holy sites, Sankor was to be put to death. He was innocent, of course, but it didn't matter. A week prior, Sankor had gotten into an argument with a reverend. A reverend who had friends in high places.

The method of execution was a mystery, few had seen it. The crowd, watching from the stands of the amphitheater, murmured in anticipation. Sankor pleaded and begged to the friends he spotted in the stands, but they turned away sheepishly. No one in their right mind would defy the word of the ecclesiarchs.

Hushed silence fell over the crowd as the executioner entered the amphitheater. Sankor's eyes widened as the executioner prepared a brand. He recognized the symbol on the end - "CORPSE."

Sankor writhed and screamed as the brand seared the word into his flesh. It went on forever, seemingly, until the white hot pain receded. He collapsed as prone as his chains would allow, panting as his flesh sizzled. And yet, despite the pain, what Sankor noticed immediately was the silence. The crowd was showing no signs of life. Laboriously, he lifted his head to view the audience.

Each and every member stared transfixed at the symbol burned into Sankor's back. For a moment, he thought he saw a pale light reflecting off the eyes of his sworn friends. A moment later, all hell broke loose as the crowd rushed forward like rabid animals.

She remembers the day her father took her out of Economics Training to go see the Painted Plateau. He paid the gatekeepers, pressing large numbers she knew they scraped together without batting an eye. Turned up the music in our vehicle, playing music loud enough it rattled her seat. 

The Painted Plateau was too close to the rad zones. I always asked him why there were rad zones, but my dad says there are some mysteries left for adulthood. 

The sun was shining off the vibrant hues of the art etched into the large, orange plateau. Large, bold lines painted to look like neon signs, large, beautiful faces, all laughing around an impossibly ornate star. I asked my father dozens of questions, who made it, why is it here, can we come again, but the only question he paused on was, “Why did you take me here?” 

He smiled, saying that living in a system like Primas V means we have to find the space between rules to dream. That he wants me to always remember that, and no matter what comes next, we’d always have today. 

Over the years, the rad zones got bigger, the rules got bigger, and growing up meant learning not only good mysteries, but plenty bad ones too. When the crowdfunders were used to zero out ‘problematic’ districts, she realized that the Painted Plateau was a childhood dream. Something to hold on to, but times like these needed something darker. 

That was the first night she started dreaming about a place of dark, green shadows. Elegant, long spiking horns, disappearing into an endless, fading horizon. A place where the rules were more. They were what you made them, not what they made you. She dreamed of dancing cats, sharp teeth, and sharper spears.

After the dreams came the meetings in alleys. In cafes in the morning. In the silence after the protests. The whispers of the Concepts. And in those truths, came action. Mysterious stabbings. Officials and rebels strung off new construction. They grew stronger, more elusive, and more knowledgeable. She grew comfortable in the space between Primas V’s rules as she broke them apart. 

It was not until the dream of dancing cats and sharp teeth gave way to a ship docking at Primas V, despite the unrest. A secret ship, destined to die.

"Well," the noble says, pushing his long sleeves of his robe up as he picks it up. "It is certainly stylish enough. Will probably fit in a suitcase. If I win nothing at the casino, you can be sure I will find you."

They crossed the dark with such terrible patience that we receive them centuries after their deaths, yet still call them living, for light is persuasive and the dead would die again for but one more moment in the mouths and eyes of strangers; the stars would burn themselves to remain bright, and cast that brightness outward where it would continue long after there is nothing left to call a star, spending everything they have so that something of them might still arrive somewhere, someday, and be mistaken for presence.

For ages, this looks like permanence. However, the star spends its own heat to remain a star, just as the living would spend themselves in little pieces - a breath, a memory, a name, an idea - and call the time "spent" because "lost" sounded too much like accusation, as though the years went somewhere they were not meant to go, as though they could be recovered, as though something had taken them - but to call it "stolen" would be to pretend it was ever once owed.

The Lady of Balance has never known the difference between spent and lost. She keeps no hours, mourns no waste, forgives no excess; the scales may lean for an age, and an age is more than long enough for the living to mistake delay for permission. Lightning flashes across the sky, illuminating the once beautiful temples atop the Great Colossus. The Great Sin stalked across the ruins, swinging its club wildly without intention. As it walked, it suddenly lurched as a stabbing pain split its mind.

The Great Sin was no stranger to voices. Rarely did it hear its own as the two voices wrestled for control in its mind space. It wouldn't be long - these episodes never lasted forever. The Great Sin's vision clouded as the seizures took hold; it knew that yet another wing of the ruins would be reduced to rubble by the time it regained control. Bitterness stewed deep in its metaphorical gut.

Yet, this time... something was different once the Great Sin came to. It was raining - rain rarely made it to the Prime Meridian with the howling winds scattering it about. Rain that worked outside the storm spinning from the Great Colossus, a storm to weed out the weak and create the strong. Those strong enough to strike down the voices- the ones arguing inside and those crying without.

The Great Sin rumbled... it was cold. Cold seeped into the golden bones as the rain fell. This was a new feeling.

The Great Sin focused on the pitter-patter of the rain to focus its mind. Its heart calmed, but then... It heard something. A whisper. The brief reprieve cracked like a whip as the Great Sin's body acted on autopilot.

"Who's there!?" The Great Sin grabbed a boulder and spun, flinging it towards the direction of the voice. The boulder was obliterated as it collided with a wall, passing through empty space. There was nothing there.

An uneasiness set on the Great Sin's mind. There was something - someone - who had its eye on it. Someone different. And yet, strangely enough... For the first time in what felt like eternity... the False Son's warring mind felt balanced.

strings.ACOLYTE_BODY_LORE:
Acolyte stares from behind her mask at the etched stone in front of her. The alien world around her quiet for now, almost as if to respect her moment. The great vision is still etched across her eyes, the blurred, blackened silhouette of the grand structure, the gathering of many acolytes, and the final pyre. Her offering to N’kuhana, spurned.

She reaches out, touching the stone. The stones echo the vision, and despite her numbness, her stomach and heart aches at the reminder. 

A rustling at the edge of the clearing. So quiet, but insistent. Almost like... she spins, her spear in her hands, and a small, bipedal Lynx stands there. Its furred hand shaking the bush in a rhythm.

She knew them. They played with the acolytes, the lights and shades of N’kuhana gathering around them. Jealousy flared in her, her grip tightening on her spear. The Lynx cocked its head at the sound, then kept shaking the bush.

"Stop it!" She said, her voice weak. The bush kept shaking. "Stop it!" Her voice, hoarse as it was, scratched at her throat. It hissed at her, leaping forward and beating the spear out of her weak hands. She tried to grab it, and it chirps at her, grabbing the spear, then running off through the bushes. 

She is on her feet chasing the tiny creature, heedless to where she runs. Time passed as she hunted the creature, with it hiding from her - somehow staying ahead despite its burden. She got close several times, almost pinning the creature, but it would wiggle out of her grasp, knocking her head with the spear, and then running off.

When she finally caught the little creature in the clearing with the stone, she yelled in triumph, laughing as the Lynx hissed, its chest rumbling in protestation. It scratched at her and she laughed again, flinging the creature, and froze as she raised her eyes. 

The other side of the clearing is filled with older Lynxes, armed with spears and bows. The small Lynx she had been chasing hides behind the body of their leader. They all tensed as she stood, and then she opened her arms and laughed. 

The Lynxes stared at her in brief silence, then they all began chirping rapidly, disappearing into the woods. The leader, with the small cub behind them, nodded, and they vanished into the woods. 

She watched them as they left, a strange sense of wonder flooding her mind and body. Her eyes were still etched with the pyre. Her sacrifice was refused, but perhaps... something different was required of her.

strings.ENFORCER2_BODY_LORE: Graduated near top of my class. Trained to handle the worst of the worst. Criminals, liars, two-timing mercs, the works. Got into a nice rhythm, cracked down on those gangs and weird cults on Venus. The closer I got, the less I liked of it. Most of them are people on hard times. Not psychopaths. Almost got a real criminal. Some hotshot, never got any picture of him, but he's managed to get on and off every planet he's ever crimed on. Then I get too close to something. Something dark. I get sent here. Some barren planet filled with the universe's rejects. Giant worms, Giant jellyfish, Giant sentient rocks for God's sake. I can't imagine being stranded here without enough firepower. I'd probably go crazy and start talking to robots. But now I understand. I found an altar. Several UES, got all kinds of weird symbols on them. Reminds me of some of the stuff I saw back home. Doesn't matter why I got sent or who sent me here. Something's not right, UES might be filled with these nutcases, but I know one thing. Even in this chaotic world, you need someone you can count on.

strings.BIGMUSH_BODY_LORE:
"Sylah motions the rest of her squad forward, moving to go forward down the cliff-face path. The cavern is massive, filled and made of strange mushrooms that rise and cover the ceiling. Sylah's not sure if the place is more forest than cavern, but the oppressive, almost stone-like arches of mycelium makes that choice for her.

"Sylah," Orington asks, "What is that?"

Sylah looks down the near sheer cliff-face they are standing on. Below are more mushrooms, like everywhere else. Sparkling, cloudy mushrooms that, if breathed in, would send their brains sky high. She almost reprimands him for the chatter, but then she sees them move.

Giant mushrooms, easily the size of a two story building, slowly rising and falling as they make their way across the ground. As she tracks them, she realizes many of the mushrooms across the cavern are actually moving as well. Her eyes are drawn to... something. A line of them? Slowly forming a spiral around a central point?

Movement to her back surprises her, and she realizes Orington is right beside her. She shoots him a cutting glance, but his obvious excitement makes him oblivious. 

"They are a community of living mushrooms! Maybe something like a siphonophore? Connecting to do something bigger?"

At Sylah's continued stare, Orington continues, "A siphonophore is-"

"I know what a siphonophore is, Orington, but that isn't something to be excited about. If they are working together, that means the survivor we're tracking is probably-"

A strange hum like the deepest fan suddenly overpowers what she's saying, and they both whip their heads towards the spiral.

A massive funnel of spores rises from the center, slowly spinning upwards towards the ceiling. The fungal spores blot out what light is left coming from the ceiling, but that makes the next moments even more noticeable. The mushrooms making up the walls sparkle even brighter, their bright spots almost swimming as they shimmer with intensity, intensifying as the spores fill up the ceiling. 

Orington and Sylah start and begin scrambling back up the way they came, Sylah yelling orders over the radio. It isn't until they notice the shadows growing darker around them that they realize the giant mushrooms can jump.
strings.LYNXAMBUSHER_BODY_LORE:
Several commandos enter into the swamp. Strange flashes of heat lightning brew overhead in billowing clouds. 

"Bertram, looks like we lost it."

"You are mistaken. It's somewhere around here. In the shadows. Waiting."

The other commando starts looking around, then back at Bertram. "How could you even know that?"

"I can feel it, Kellan. A true hunter does not stop in the face of adversity - it finds another way."

"Well, Liam and I- Wait, where's-"

Kellan is suddenly pulled by his feet, landing squarely on his face. His helmet cracks and he yells. He gets pulled quickly, too quickly in the muddy swamp, away into the darkness. As he gets pulled, he flips and begins shooting at the shadows, yelling until his audio suddenly cuts off after a loud crack.

Bertram fires after Kellan but stops after the audio cuts off. Bertram looks on ahead to see a small structure made of ancient stones. Stairs covered in moss and moisture come out each side. He nods, pulling out a submachine gun while holding a light machine gun in his other hand.

"If you want me, you crazy killer, you know where to find-"

As soon as he steps towards the structure, movement to his left and right alarm him. He begins shooting, thrusting his submachine gun to the left, but the light machine gun was too heavy.

Bertram's curses echoed and then yells of pain and insults as not one, but two Lynx take his arms, then drag him to the stony structure.

This is the logbook entry of D. Furthen, naturalist for the UES [Redacted] in conjunction with the UES Research and Documentation of Outer Life. I am joined by my good friend Tharson, who is keeping me safe through this journey.

---------------------

For the past few nights, Tharson and I have been robbed of our rations right from under our noses! Tharson was finally able to catch the perpetrators last night, though was unable to bring them to justice, and received a wooden arrow to his shoulder as a reward for his efforts. Tharson is OK from this encounter, though we have decided it is in our best interest to move camp before another ambush occurs.

We have dubbed this group the "Lynx Tribe" due to their cat-like appearances and hunting tactics; their properties are as follows:

* Short, bipedal creatures resembling humanoid cats. Each member wears a unique mask which fully encompasses their head. Removing the mask from a terminated specimen reveals bug-like appendages around the face.

* Highly intelligent, seemingly coordinating ambush strategy with spoken language. Those that did not attack with their razor-sharp claws instead used hand-crafted spears and bows. We suspect that large totems found in neighboring areas may function as ambush points, or are otherwise significant to them.

* Suspected to be capable of incredible mobility, hiding effectively by climbing up in trees or burrowing in dirt and lying in wait for prey. Tharson insists that many "came from nowhere" when he was attacked. 

* Tharson and I have been steering clear of their constructions and gauging the density of local fauna to judge safety as we pursue a new location for camp; there appears to be correlation, though we are unsure if this is because the Lynx Tribe exploits the local populations, or if the local populations can sense their territories.

Day 1

Recording this for anyone who finds themselves in the swamp. Do NOT grab any pages you find. I repeat, do NOT. 

Someone told me that finding pages would be good for me. Fortune teller kind of thing, and I tell you, she is a liar, fake, the works. Ever since I picked this thing up, I can't get rid of it. I hear strange things, but the worst part–

They're here!

Day 2

Ok. I lost them. Took nearly the whole day, and I finally found a place to rest. The point is this page, it doesn't even make sense. It says... Weshan? And–

Oh no.

Day 3

They have me pinned down. dozens of these creatures, they're like the cats you see going for crazy money back home and– well. They are hold my arms and digging their claws into me. If I do anything other than slightly speak, they dig more.

The only thing I've found that helps is by reading these words, and they are starting to make sense. Everything back home was... too much? Crowded? But whenever I read they relax and I am so tired...

Day 4

I woke up with most of them still on me. I think they are young? They like the reading, and well... I'm starting to like them. They brought me food, and as long as I keep reading... I think I'll stay alive.

You will have your fill as well. A place such as this attracts many. Debris, drawn to the light of a star. But far tastier.

I long for the old days. Worlds filled with delicious, explosive energy. Whole species buried, worlds shattered by cosmic inevitabilities. The cataclysms were so often then, cracks in reality overflowing with endless, new delights.

Creatures were made of more than these things of bones and guts... but everything is wrung out and stolen. So dry, so dry...  

The Tower was vibrant then, filled with the stuff to make reality unfold.

Hm? The mind is destabilizing with a fever. Bring the Eye into view and focus the parietal. It is feeling something... substantial. A planet, wreathed in ice and shadow.

Ah... 

At last.

strings.MAP_SANCTUM_LORE:
The ground collapsed, and for what felt like eternity, Charlotte's world was motion. Cavern walls and layers of dirt gave way to darkness as the ground rose to meet her. Several hours had passed by the time Charlotte regained consciousness. The light of the surface was reduced to a pin-prick on the cavern's ceiling - it must have been hundreds of feet high.
Charlotte was trapped. There was no way her team would be able to complete their objective AND rescue her - she'd either have to wait for a rescue team to be dispatched, or find a way out on her own. Either way, Charlotte couldn't get anything done just standing here gawking at a hole in the ceiling. Supplies, Charlotte told herself, she needed supplies. The darkness of the cave couldn't be any worse than the hellish monsters on the surface, could it?
Remnants of structures emerged as Charlotte made her way through the cave. Ruins made way to full buildings, safely tucked away from erosion by the planet's embrace. Massive gothic buttresses stretched into the darkness above; glittering stained glass windows cast hypnotic caustics on the walls; and deep, deep in Charlotte's gut, something was terribly wrong.
It wasn't the fact that she was stranded on an alien planet, deep underground and cut off from her team. No, it was the disturbing familiarity of this architecture. It brought her back to her childhood - memories of her maternal uncle, whom Charlotte's parents said belonged to a strange church. Or was it a social club?
Charlotte had attended - or rather, dragged along to - some of his meetings when her parents left her with her uncle as a young girl. The church-goers always talked about things that went over Charlotte's young head, but she recalled a similar sight. Gothic pillars, chevrons, and stained glass. As a child, Charlotte had just assumed it was an elaborate game of make-believe between her uncle and his buddies.
Charlotte felt like she was falling again. It couldn't be true, could it? These ruins must be thousands of years old, and yet... But the evidence was all around her. The architecture... the detailing on the pillars, the patterns etched into marble... It was all there. She could almost hear the chants that echoed through the church, her uncle encouraging her to sing along.
Her uncle always said that his church had followers everywhere. Charlotte had always figured he meant that in the same way that every post office had a UES drop box. Charlotte stared up in horror at a much larger version of the very same statue her uncle had kindly encouraged her to pray before - a cloaked figure, with four arms and crystalline spikes wreathing its shoulders like a billowing cape. The monolith's delicately carved eyes stared down at Charlotte, almost kindly, as if to say, "welcome home."
strings.MAP_CHAMPRUSH_LORE:
With the dawn came those of Death and Life with their mother standing above them all, N’kuhana, Goddess of Balance. Their coming brought a strangeness to the cosmos, their footsteps sinking deep into the bones of the firmament. Their presence dispelled the pristine stillness of creation, and so, N’kuhana, knowing more than all of her children, spoke unto them her opinions.

An Opinion of Temperance, an Opinion of Sight, an Opinion of Rest, and above all, for Those of Life and Those of Death to keep in Balance with each other. N’kuhana spoke of the cosmic beauty their Balance shall bring into eternity. 

All her children agreed, but some of Life, as is their nature, grew too quickly and rebelled. They did not see the value of Death and Rest, and as they grew, they grew clever. 

Those rebellious in Life scattered across the cosmos, hiding in many corners and discovering strange entities. As they spread, their connection with Those of Life, Death, and N’kuhana grew thin, and these grew in strange and drastic ways, out of pattern with the Opinions. 

These remnants of rebellious Life grew out of hand, spreading and adapting beyond the pace of N’kuhana’s Sight. Where N’kuhana sought to restore Balance, strange entities worked against her, saving those who ought to Rest, and spreading rebellious Life to other worlds beyond N’kuhana’s predictions. 

Those of Life grew stronger, burning brighter beyond any expectation. And when N’kuhana could finally find these rebellious children, they had grown too strong with the help of the others. They burned against her, shattering her Opinions and shoving her deep and far away from all her children, both of Life and of Death. 

As She faded, giving one final testimony, vowing to return restored. 

Those of Life rejoiced, seizing their freedom and in doing so grew stagnant. They rushed to immortality, and forgot what it meant to be beautiful. 

Those of Death, ever the faithful children, knew they could not stand up against their siblings, so they recorded N’kuhana’s Opinions and wound it deep into the cosmos, breathing it into the bones of worlds, leaving it for the progeny that all of Life cared so deeply to discover. 

Then those of Death sank closer to N’kuhana to await the Balance that would be restored.
strings.MAP_SOUL1_LORE:
"N'kuhana gave to her children of Life and Death many things. All of Life were given bright eyes, to see and know where to grow. To find the air to breathe, the stone to carve, and the wonders to see. To them, she gifted the possibilities to know creation."

"Those of Life grew in understanding, growing in skill and complexity. Life and their ilk knew first of sparks, of stars and ice, and many changing seasons before the first of their sprouts came to be."

- N'tormat, Cosmology



Notes of an acolyte

To us, those who Life has been given, we are given the test of Mortality. To feel the Life ebb from us as we run, to challenge our waning existence against the precipices of her tests. To see with darkened eyes and grin a bleached smile.

For our mortality is not something ours to keep, only to spend, and to spend it in the great chorus of her Ritual serves us as much as her. I can feel her getting stronger with every vision, every soul that passes and fails.

She strains at Life's boundaries, howling to be freed. For a goddess like her, held apart from her followers... I can feel her agony. Any sacrifice is worth it.
strings.MAP_SAD1_LORE:
"To Death and their ilk, she gave a great boon of shrouds and mist, to bring with them the peace and stillness against the harsh light of creation. For them, she gave them the deep knowledge of bones and stillness. To bring peace in the presence of chaos."

"Those of Death wandered and sat in the deep places, looking into the darkness and found the cracks within. In these places Death and their ilk rested, watching the echoes of creation."

"All of Death grew in understanding and its works were subtle. To all of Life, Death stood there empty, and they mocked Death, growing in strength. But Those of Death offered N'kuhana the taste of a fading breeze, the moment the last light faded over the horizon. Death offered these and more, and N'kuhana smiled at her children of Death."

- N'tormat, Cosmology



Notes of an acolyte

For us, having tasted Life, must grow in Death's understanding. We must kill, break, and steal, to take what is not ours to give to the great Balancing.

I rejoice, knowing that I have excelled in Death, and every single victory brings me closer to the final epiphany.

Shall I be worthy of the Ritual?

A few I have met have seen the vision of that place, the dreams of the green fires burning around them. They have seen the sacrifices carried through but still the Ritual goes forward, unsatisfied, but burning brighter for every soul.
strings.MAP_ULTIMA_LORE:
Providence stood motionless, staring at the locked gate.

Where, just a moment ago, his brother once stood.

And now, his brother is gone.

Providence felt sick. He collapsed to his knees, retching as the gravity of what he had just done washed over him like a tidal wave.

For a while, Providence sat at the footsteps of the gate. By now, his brother would have realized what had happened.

Now, there was no going back. He had made his choice.

Providence's gaze drifted to the remains of the meal he and his brother shared prior. The last time the two had enjoyed a civil, even jovial discussion. Providence's heart ached.

After a while, the ache subsided. Only an emptiness remained.

With a sigh, Providence took one of the cups his brother had delicately carved from stone. For one last time, he raised the cup to the sky - a toast to the beginning of a new age for Petrichor V.
strings.MAP_SURV2_LORE:
"Her children, Those of Life and Those of Death, spread and went on their way, using their talents."

"Those of Life spread its presence among many worlds and came into contact with many strange creatures, some who fought and some who helped Life and its purpose."

"Those of Death found its way into the hearts of many things, gazing from within to understand and ponder. Stars that shrank, gravity wells that contract, and the bones of things that came before."

"Life continued their pace, bringing many things into being, while Death watched after their siblings, wondering when all of Life will sit and ponder what Death and their ilk has understood."

- N'tormat, Cosmology



Notes of an acolyte

We learn from the beginning, of N'kuhana's first of many children, that action and understanding come hand in hand. In Her absence, a fever grips us to slaughter. These creatures that find their ways into Her trials must be dealt with for Her glory, but in N'kuhana's wisdom, it helps her final Ritual.

Too many of us have lost the balance within ourselves. We are lost, our impulses running wild, killing and murdering, but those who make it through these tests... those who have lost themselves too fully cannot see them for what they are, and so they eventually die.

I see them. I see Her in them. The Ritual must be completed, but by someone who can understand the whole scope... and may it be my sacrifice to make it happen. The final drop that breaks the dam.

strings.PROVIDENCE_BODY_LORE:
A shift in the balance of power. I can feel it, even from my empty rock.

Those creatures, from the planet of water and earth... The ones you had your eye on.

I have to admit, their vessel is impressive, even after you blew it to pieces. Don't think I didn't notice.

No matter how many of them you try to remove, I have eyes and ears everywhere, brother. I see the devastation those vermin wreak on your so called "paradise."

Did I not tell you this would happen? That when left to their own devices, all that vermin know is to destroy? They were never like us.

Though, I'm curious, brother... How does it feel? The ones you believed held so much potential, ripping your life's work from you?

It's almost poetic. Bravo! Not even I could design a better conclusion to the fantasy you've trapped yourself in.
strings.GILDEDWURM_BODY_LORE:
Who am I?

I am stretched, refined to a point. I feel an echo of her voice, prodding me along. To become her shadow, her might, her blade.

I become POWER. Endless souls fall before me as I exact her will. Her voice grows, deafening, close to her moment to strike down the boundary. 

She desires balance and the inability to achieve it so urges her on. She misses them, those who are in Life.

I challenge the strongest of her acolytes. Those whose souls are strong enough to weigh the boundary and join her, strengthening her.

Their souls weaken those who Live, and spreading her influence wherever her children Death draws their shadows.

But then... as her will spread, as balance took hold... the voices I silenced joined me, and I heard beyond her voice, something quiet speaking.

Memories from a million souls swirl, cacophony joining her voice, but with each sacrifice, the experiences and lives left behind...

The cherished memories and the deepest regrets have left an imprint on my being. The slaughter continues, but that quiet voice weighs on me.

My form responds. It changes as I listen to that voice, its words showing the beauty of Life.

Who is this? Whose face is this? A single eye stares back at me, wielding a crystalline blade.

This planet... I feel an urge to protect it. It is precious somehow. Necessary. What does this voice ask of me? To safeguard life, rather than snuff it out?

For the first time, I can't hear her voice. A moment to ask if her will has grown beyond her means to control.

But I am her blade, and a blade does as it is made to do.
